readingMode: All 19 physical pages read sequentially in full, including cover, manifesto, every bullet and back cover. Original pages 1 and 10 visually inspected. No annex or endnote.
territorialScope: León España Vaciada 23J programme; applies to the León ballot only. The five-constituency result denomination also includes Asturias, Palencia, Salamanca and Valladolid, requiring their own adoption or programme records. Separate EV-PCAS-TC Burgos coalition never inherits this local programme automatically.

coverage.authoredAnalysis: Read the whole cover: León España Vaciada, programme for the 23J general election, version V06_07. Original visual inspection confirms the fragmented native logo text.
Read the entire manifesto. The programme identifies León and territorial depopulation as its focus. Population figures and promised outcomes are attributed claims, not independently certified facts.

Read both development proposals: legislation to rebalance opportunities and a State depopulation pact with positive social, entrepreneurial and fiscal measures. No single nationwide tax amount is specified here.

Read all health proposals: primary care at 25% of the public health budget, guaranteed local professional care per health zone, doubled nursing ratio and urgent ambulance attendance within 30 minutes. Do not convert attendance into travel time to any hospital.

Read national access-to-high-capacity-road aspiration, five named León-related road projects and elimination of AP66/AP71 tolls. These are separate propositions, not support for removing every Spanish toll.

Read rail renovation to 160–200 km/h, two high-speed lines, FEVE integration/frequencies/service modernisation, winter ski connection and ten daily services each direction on three named routes. Local investment priorities do not establish all national rail funding choices.

Read every connectivity bullet: fibre and 5G wherever people live by 2024, rural perspective in telecommunications law, broadband planning and technology for rural work/agriculture. Universal coverage does not state zero consumer price.

Read every economy bullet: 25% income-tax reduction for self-employed people in León, 30-euro monthly contribution up to 2,000 euros monthly income with progressive charges above it, corporate rate 17.5% in León and sustainable decentralised industrial estates. Tax scope and contribution condition matter.

Read every territorial bullet: neighbourhood council powers, decentralising administration/public-company headquarters by demographic criteria, young León return plan, national rural housing activation and banking access. No forced sale, blanket expropriation or free home is specified.

Read all energy bullets and inspected the complete original page. Supports renewables with local conditions, community generation and 20% grid-node access reserved to communities. Energy projects require 25% local participation, training/hiring and a printed 15% per generated kilowatt-hour levy; levy base is unclear.

Read every energy continuation bullet: small hydro recovery, forest biomass, more efficient wind repowering and waste biogas. The text says 'asistentes parques'; preserve the original typo and do not derive a ban on new turbines.

Read the territory-custody tax from consuming to producing territories, legal personality for the Cantabrian mountain range, sustainable forest/grazing/resource management and groundwater protection through irrigation modernisation and revised reservoir compensation. Do not infer an exact tax rate.

Read all people-care proposals: autonomy and ageing at home through mixed home/residential support, essential home help available 24 hours with income-proportional copayments, and services for gender-violence victims and children. Copayment means the home-help proposal is not free for everyone.

Read rural migrant reception/integration, better care-home inspection, maternity leave of 32 weeks including pregnancy sickness classification, and employer incentives for remote work. Maternity wording does not explicitly grant 32 weeks to both parents.

Read every tourism bullet: provincial competitiveness, Picos de Europa sustainability, Bierzo wine tourism, international biosphere-reserve promotion, San Marcos expansion and living museums. Do not substitute this targeted programme for all tourism regulation.

Read every agriculture bullet: extensive livestock, conditional macrofarm moratorium pending livestock censuses, local/organic food in public meals, agricultural climate adaptation and young farmer support. The moratorium is conditional rather than a permanent universal ban.

Read rural vocational training, free compulsory-school textbooks, a children's literature festival, local cultural events and reopening Teatro Emperador. Textbooks do not imply free university tuition or every private-school expense.

Read the entire final policy page: local participation in El Teleno shooting-range management, limits on home-delivered electoral advertising/equal sustainable material use and cooperation among minor local entities. No military-base closure is promised.
Read the whole back cover, identifying León España Vaciada and the party URL. No appendix, endnote or further policy text.

uncertainties: Numeric positions remain null until full corpus cross-reference, authored propositions/rubrics and independent calibration.
Local tax rates and road/rail projects retain León applicability; do not generalise to every España Vaciada ballot.
Energy levy percentage denominator is unclear despite faithful native extraction and original visual confirmation.
Maternity leave wording is gender-specific; no automatic equal 32-week entitlement for both parents.
Macrofarm moratorium depends on livestock censuses; textbooks are compulsory-school only; home help has income-proportional copayments.
authorship: Direct complete programme reading and English analysis with original literal Spanish excerpts; deterministic extraction/hash/quote/schema checks only, no question or position generator.
